title: Nucleotide dependency analysis of DNA language models reveals genomic functional elements
summary: Nucleotide-dependency maps derived from genomic-language-model probabilities identified four candidate regulatory RNA structures upstream of E. coli genes; the study reports experimental validation by DMS-MaPseq. The model also highlighted regulatory motifs and variant effects.
ai_technology: Genomic language models estimate nucleotide probabilities; pairwise dependency maps expose functional motifs and RNA contacts that guided discovery of four previously unreported E. coli RNA structures.
organization: University of California San Diego; University of California, Berkeley

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; primary publication record or first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: The v1 manuscript reports four predicted structures followed by DMS-MaPseq experiments; it compares model-derived structure and variant-effect signals with existing approaches.
evidence.unknown: The evidence is from one study and specific E. coli genes; no separate-team replication was identified.
evidence.ai_role: Genomic language models estimate nucleotide probabilities; pairwise dependency maps expose functional motifs and RNA contacts that guided discovery of four previously unreported E. coli RNA structures.
